as_told.title: 2010 F.E. Warren missile shutdown attributed to cigar-shaped object

tellings.quote: On October 23, 2010, F.E. Warren Air Force Base, in Cheyenne, Wyoming, temporarily lost the ability to communicate with 50 of its Minuteman III nuclear missiles. The five Missile Alert Facilities responsible for launching those ICBMs in time of war—Alpha through Echo, comprising the 319th Strategic Missile Squadron—would have been unable to do so during the period of the disruption.
The Air Force then quickly acknowledged the problem, saying that a back-up system could have launched the missiles and claiming that the breakdown had lasted a mere 59 minutes.

However, the latter statement was untrue, according to two missile technicians stationed at F.E. Warren, who say that the communications problem, while intermittent, actually persisted over several hours.

tellings.page: section "The Military Sightings on October 23–24, 2010", paragraph 4
tellings.quote: On October 23–24, 2010, one or more "huge" cigar-shaped objects were observed by active duty Air Force personnel in the field.

tellings.page: section "The Military Sightings on October 23–24, 2010", paragraph 6
tellings.quote: I would guess it was 7:1, or seven [units] long to one [unit] wide, or so it looked. It was tapered on both ends and very big.

I emphasize that the aforementioned confidential sources at the base have not said that the UFO(s) sighted actually caused the disruption, and it must be noted that the Air Force's Global Strike Command has now officially attributed the problem to an improperly-replaced circuit card in a weapons-system processor.

plain: In October 2010, the story goes, F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming lost contact with dozens of its nuclear missiles while staff saw strange craft in the sky, which Michels ties to a Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. Michels tells it often, drawing on the researcher Robert Hastings, author of UFOs and Nukes, and on a Wired article about the outage: he says key personnel made several independent sightings during a power failure, that the outage lasted about an hour, and that on-site sources link it to objects that "seem to break physics". In one episode he calls the object cigar-shaped instead, gives the outage as 59 minutes, and says President Obama was briefed. Hastings's article, published June 21, 2011, says that on October 23, 2010 the base "temporarily lost the ability to communicate with 50 of its Minuteman III nuclear missiles", and that while the Air Force said it lasted "a mere 59 minutes", two missile technicians said it "persisted over several hours". He writes that "one or more 'huge' cigar-shaped objects" were seen by Air Force personnel, one described as about seven times as long as wide. He also stresses that his sources "have not said that the UFO(s) sighted actually caused the disruption", and that the Air Force blamed "an improperly-replaced circuit card". So the article speaks of a huge cigar-shaped craft rather than a Tic Tac, and the step from an object seen that day to the cause of the outage is the tellers' reading, one Hastings says his sources did not make. If true, unexplained craft were present while US nuclear missiles were knocked offline.

discussion.by: Huge UFO Sighted Near Nuclear Missiles During October 2010 Launch System Disruption
discussion.text: Hastings writes that on 23 and 24 October 2010 "one or more “huge” cigar-shaped objects were observed by active duty Air Force personnel in the field", which a retired technician put at about seven times as long as wide, likened to a Zeppelin; and that the outage "actually persisted over several hours", where the Air Force said 59 minutes. He adds: "I emphasize that the aforementioned confidential sources at the base have not said that the UFO(s) sighted actually caused the disruption", and that Global Strike Command attributed it to "an improperly-replaced circuit card". The object in this article is a huge, Zeppelin-like craft where the tellers speak of a Tic Tac, and the step from an object seen on the day of the outage to the object behind it is the tellers' reading, which Hastings says his sources did not make.
